input: In this example, we are going to calculate the Reynolds number for water flowing in a pipe, and then use the result to say what the flow regime is. The Reynolds number Re (dimensionless) is calculated from the density rho (kg m-3), the mean velocity v (m s-1), the pipe diameter D (m) and the dynamic viscosity mu (Pa s) by means of the expression Re = rho v D / mu. For water at 293 K, the density is rho = 998 kg m-3 and the viscosity is mu = 1.00 x 10-3 Pa s. The pipe diameter is D = 0.05 m and the mean velocity is v = 1.9 m s-1. If we substitute these values into the expression, the numerator works out at 998 x 1.9 x 0.05 = 94.81, and dividing this by the viscosity, taken as 0.001 Pa s, gives us Re = 94800. To decide the flow regime, we compare this value with the usual thresholds: the flow is laminar below Re = 2300 and turbulent above Re = 4000, while between these two values the regime is transitional and cannot be assigned from the number alone. Since our calculated value of 94800 is very much greater than 4000, the flow in this case is clearly turbulent, and the transitional band between 2300 and 4000 does not come into the decision at all. So the answer to the example is that the Reynolds number comes out at 94800 and the regime is turbulent, the value of 94800 lying far above the transitional band that begins at 2300.

The Reynolds number Re (dimensionless) is computed from the density rho (kg m-3), the mean velocity v (m s-1), the pipe diameter D (m) and the dynamic viscosity mu (Pa s) by Re = rho v D / mu. Water at 293 K has rho = 998 kg m-3 and mu = 1.00 x 10-3 Pa s; the pipe diameter D is 0.05 m and the mean velocity v is 1.9 m s-1. Substitution gives the numerator as 998 x 1.9 x 0.05 = 94.81, and division by the viscosity, taken as 0.001 Pa s, gives Re = 94800. The regime is read from the thresholds. Flow is laminar below Re = 2300 and turbulent above Re = 4000; between the two values the regime is transitional and is not assigned by the number alone. The computed value, 94800, stands above the upper threshold by a wide margin, so the assignment does not rest on the transitional range at all: the value is in the turbulent region under the stated thresholds, and no part of the check depends on behaviour between 2300 and 4000. The check on the result is the threshold comparison itself. A value below 2300 would be laminar, a value between the thresholds would stay unassigned, and the value obtained, 94800, is turbulent. The example also shows the order in which such a check is made: the number is computed from the four stated quantities, each with its unit, and only then compared with the thresholds, because the thresholds are values of the same number and the comparison is meaningless until the number stands on the same basis. The threshold that decides this case is the upper one, 4000, and the computed value clears it without qualification.
